2026.intro: The 2026 regulations are a complete reset of chassis, aerodynamics and power units — nothing from 2025 carries over.

cards.title: Active aerodynamics replace DRS
cards.body: Movable front and rear wings open on straights (**Straight Mode**) to cut drag and close in corners (**Corner Mode**) for downforce — every driver, every lap. Straight-line speed and cornering grip are no longer a simple trade-off.

cards.title: 50/50 power split
cards.body: Close to equal power from the combustion engine and the MGU-K (around 350 kW of electrical power). The battery depletes fast, so cars harvest energy for stretches of every lap — **energy management software is now as decisive as hardware**.

cards.title: Overtake Mode
cards.body: Within one second of the car ahead at the detection point, a driver gets extra electrical deployment that works in corners too — overtakes now build across sequences of corners, not just down one straight.

cards.title: Power unit manufacturers
cards.body: Audi arrives as a works team, Red Bull build their own engine with Ford (RB Powertrains), and Honda returns as Aston Martin's exclusive supplier.

cards.title: Cadillac — the 11th team
cards.body: General Motors' Cadillac joins as the first new team since 2016, running Ferrari power with **Sergio Pérez** and **Valtteri Bottas**.

cards.title: Tighter power unit allocation
cards.body: Each driver may use 4 engines, 4 turbochargers, 4 exhaust sets, 3 MGU-Ks, 3 energy stores, 3 control electronics units and 6 of each ancillary component in 2026 (Sporting Regulations B8.2.2 plus one extra of each for the first season). Going over costs 10 grid places the first time for each element, 5 for each one after. Live usage per driver is in Team Pace Profiles → Component usage.

aduo.explainer: **Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities** let a power unit manufacturer whose combustion engine is at least 2% down on the best one make extra upgrades to its homologated engine. The FIA measures an **ICE performance index** — built from engine torque, engine speed, MGU-K power and how sensitive lap time is to power — over set review periods. It targets engine power only, not championship position: a team can be low in the standings and get nothing if its engine is competitive.

thresholds.budget: up to $11m, plus up to $8m of future cost cap brought forward (2026 only)

aduo.thresholdsNote: Budget figures are extra cost-cap allowance per review period. Qualifying also brings extra dyno testing time.

periods.name: Period 1
periods.result: Mercedes 2–4% behind (1 extra homologation in 2026 + 1 in 2027). Audi, Ferrari and Honda more than 4% behind (2 in 2026 + 2 in 2027).

periods.name: Period 2
periods.result: No additional homologations granted to any manufacturer.

manufacturers.note: Not granted any ADUO — its engine was within 2% of the best in both periods. The FIA doesn't name the benchmark engine.
